text.visual_description: The scene core of this image features a close-up of a clenched fist, indicating tension or frustration. The character's hand is prominent, with a yellow sweater visible, suggesting it belongs to a cartoon figure.
text.usage_text: Arthur's Fist, also known as Clenched Fist, is a reaction image featuring a screen capture of the protagonist Arthur from the titular children's television series holding a clenched fist, which is often accompanied by captions describing various infuriating or frustrating circumstances. The image is taken from the Arthur Punches D.W. scene, notable for inspiring a series of YouTube poop videos.

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image features Spider-Man lying in a hospital bed with a slightly indifferent expression. He is propped up with pillows, and his right hand rests on his chest while the left arm is under the blanket.
text.usage_text: I Don't Need a Doctor, X Will Save Me refers to a series of memes based on the image of 60's Spider-Man lying in a hospital bed that humorously imagine how various socioeconomic groups would argue for or against a doctor attending to them. Originating from a viral 2018 post, the format gained a significant presence on iFunny in late February 2020.

text.visual_description: The scene features a well-dressed man in a suit standing at a podium with microphones, holding his hand to his ear as if trying to hear something better. The background includes flags that suggest a formal setting.
text.usage_text: Barack Obama is an American politician who served as the 44th President of the United States after entering the office in January 2009 and left in January 2017 when Donald Trump became the 45th President. He was the first and only African American ever to hold the office of Presidency in the history of the United States.

text.visual_description: The scene features a statue resembling a historical religious figure, with long hair and a beard. The statue is in a lively pose, pointing towards the viewer with one hand, while giving a thumbs-up with the other.
text.usage_text: Buddy Christ refers to a scene from the Kevin Smith film "Dogma" in which a cardinal attempts to rebrand Jesus Christ to attract new converts to the Catholic Church. The Buddy Christ is a smiling, cartoonish depiction of Jesus Christ who is holding both hands up, giving the thumbs up, and winking.

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image features a tabby cat sitting at a countertop, appearing as if it is resting its forepaws on the surface in a manner similar to a human resting their arms. There are no actions taking place aside from the cat’s poised sitting position.
text.usage_text: Chris Hansen Cat is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photo of a cat positioned as if it is seated at a table, accompanied by feline-related puns and LOLcat jokes. The macros often begin with the phrase "Why don't you have a seat," popularized by Chris Hansen, the former host of the reality TV series To Catch a Predator.

text.visual_description: The scene features a man in the foreground set against a snowy mountainous background. He is dressed in winter hiking gear, including a yellow and blue jacket and a backpack with visible straps.
text.usage_text: "Better Drink My Own Piss" is an image macro series featuring a photo of Edward "Bear" Grylls, the host of the UK's wildlife survival series Born Survivor, also known as Man vs. Wild in the US, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. While some macros use captions parodying the ridiculous and oftentimes unnecessary stunts Grylls performs on the show, they typically focus on the consumption of his own urine.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts a group of animated characters, prominently featuring a pink starfish-like entity in the foreground, who is engaged in dramatic gesturing. The top half shows the starfish with arms outstretched, seemingly giving an animated explanation or making a point.
text.usage_text: Push It Somewhere Else Patrick (also known as "Pushing Patrick") is an image macro series based on a scene from the animated television series SpongeBob SquarePants. The captions typically use the snowclone template "We should take X and put it Y" or "We should X and Y" to suggest an alternative solution to a given problem.

text.visual_description: The image depicts a single koala positioned against a tree trunk with a leafy background, holding and chewing a eucalyptus leaf. There are no visible text elements in the image.
text.usage_text: The Koala Copypasta refers to a 2016 Reddit comment in which a person viciously insults koala bears and their numerous poor biological functions, beginning with "Koalas are fucking horrible animals." The vitriol with which the person expresses their distaste for koalas amused social media, leading the comment to grow into a copypasta that some people debate and refute when reposted.

text.visual_description: The image features a close-up of a fish, likely an eel, with prominent eyes and an open mouth. There are no other characters or entities visible, making the eel the singular subject.
text.usage_text: Bad Joke Eel is an advice animal image macro series featuring a close-up photograph of a moray eel with various captions delivering unfunny puns and jokes, very similar to Lame Pun Coon.

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image features a young child dressed in a formal black tuxedo, complete with a bow tie. The child is captured in the act of pointing aggressively with a slightly furrowed brow, conveying a sense of assertiveness or demand.
text.usage_text: Baby Godfather is an image macro series featuring a scowling baby dressed in a tuxedo with a bow tie, pointing to the ground with his index finger. The captions typically portray the baby as an infant version of Don Corleone, a fictional mafia boss character in Mario Puzo's novel and Francis Coppola's film adaptation, The Godfather.

text.visual_description: The image depicts a group at what appears to be a beach or poolside setting. The main characters include four young women in bikinis and one young man in casual attire seated with a laptop.
text.usage_text: Priority Peter is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photograph of a teenage boy holding a calculator surrounded by several young women wearing bathing suits. The captions typically consist of puns involving mathematical jargon and suggestive double entendres, some of which are set up so the last word in the top caption rhymes with the last word in the bottom caption.

text.visual_description: The scene features two animated fish characters in a sequence of four panels. The main character is a large, muscular fish with an intimidating demeanor, while the second character is smaller with a headband labeled "MOM." In the first panel, the large fish looks angry and dominates the frame, while the smaller fish appears to be saying something.
text.usage_text: Welcome to the Salty Spitoon. How Tough Are Ya? refers to a series of memes based on a scene from SpongeBob SquarePants in which a fish wishing to enter a pub proves his toughness to a bouncer with a personal anecdote. The format is typically used to present various deeds as impressive and tough feats, whether genuine or sarcastic in nature.

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image features a character resembling a sponge-like creature, known for being expressive and animated. The character is bent forward with knees slightly bent, arms held out in a slightly awkward posture, giving a sense of exaggerated mimicry or parody.
text.usage_text: Mocking SpongeBob, also known as SpongeMock, refers to an image macro featuring the cartoon character SpongeBob SquarePants, in which people use a picture of SpongeBob to indicate a mocking tone towards an opinion or point of view.

text.visual_description: The image depicts a simple black-and-white cartoon face, drawn with thick lines. The eyes are large and wide, looking upward to the left, and the mouth is small and curved into a slight, closed smile.
text.usage_text: Derp is an expression associated with stupidity, much like the earlier forms of interjections like "duh" and "dur." In image macros, the subject is typically portrayed with eyes that are pointed to each side and a caption that reads "DERP." The words "herp" and "derp" are often used in rage comics to replace nondescript names or parts of conversation. See also: Are You a Wizard.

text.visual_description: The scene features a singular character, an older green-skinned figure with large, pointed ears and a wise demeanor. The character is standing, wearing a beige robe, and their hands are clasped together in front of them.
text.usage_text: Yoda is a fictional character from the Star Wars series of films, television shows, comic books, and other forms of media. In the films, Yoda is the Jedi master and leader of the Jedi council in the Star Wars prequels. Online, Yoda, as well as his speech patterns, which typically reverse the syntax of traditional English speech, have been the subject of numerous memes.

text.visual_description: The scene core features a single animated character with a distinct red complexion, resembling a crustacean-like creature. The character is anthropomorphic, wearing a light-colored lab coat, suggesting a scientific or medical profession.
text.usage_text: Futurama Zoidberg, also known as "Why not Zoidberg?", is an advice animal image macro series featuring the cephalopod-like alien Zoidberg from the cartoon TV series Futurama. Captions typically start with a query of some sort, followed by the rhetorical question "Why not Zoidberg?" at the bottom.

text.visual_description: The scene core features a middle-aged man with a distinct mustache, wearing a brown suit and a dark tie. He is in a professional-looking environment with paintings in the background.
text.usage_text: Ron Swanson is a character from the NBC sitcom Parks and Recreation. Played by Nick Offerman, Ron Swanson has become notable online for his rugged demeanor and wisdom.

text.visual_description: The scene core features a young child looking directly at the viewer with a hand on their hip. The child is dressed in a matching two-piece outfit, consisting of a white top and a dark jumper, and stands in front of a mirror that slightly reflects their image.
text.usage_text: My Momma Said refers to a series of image macros in which a photograph of American recording artist Cardi B as a child. Online, people have captioned the photograph with the phrasal template beginning with "My momma said," mimicking the speech patterns and attitude of a child.

text.visual_description: The meme template consists of three panels. The first panel shows a simple cartoonish character running happily with an exaggerated smile and wide eyes, giving a cheerful thumbs-up gesture.
text.usage_text: "Nobody is Right" is an exploitable comic with easy-to-edit panels. Usually, the whole comic portrays a troll jumping in to say anything that can potentially start a flame war.

text.visual_description: The scene consists of a central character, a woman whose facial expression is exaggerated with wide eyes and mouth agape, suggesting surprise or shock. There is no visible text in this specific meme template, but the background consists of a radial pattern with alternating blue and white segments, creating a visually striking contrast that draws attention to the central figure.
text.usage_text: Annoying Facebook Girl is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photo of a teenage girl rolling her eyes with her mouth agape, accompanied by a blue and white color wheel background. The overlaid text typically depicts vapid status updates, attention-seeking behaviors, and generally irritating Facebook activity.

text.visual_description: The scene features a cartoon character standing in a doorway. The character has a round face, large, wide-open eyes, and is wearing a blue hat with a yellow pom-pom.
text.usage_text: My name is Craig Tucker. Continued: Last week was my birthday. This is a copypasta recited by the South Park character Craig Tucker in a 2008 episode of the show called "Pandemic 2: The Startling." The quote is about him getting $100 from his grandma for his birthday but then being duped by Stan, Kyle, Cartman, and Kenny into investing his money to become a Peruvian flute band with them, ultimately resulting in them being deported to Peru. The speech then turned into a copypasta in early 2023 as many TikTok users also made video content and memes that used the original audio.

name: I Have No Idea What I Am Doing

text.visual_description: The scene features a dog, specifically a Siberian Husky, sitting upright in a chair with its front paws placed on a keyboard, as if it is typing. The dog is positioned directly in front of a computer monitor, which glows with white light, suggesting the screen is on but without specific visible content.
text.usage_text: "I Have No Idea What I'm Doing" is a catchphrase often used in image macro captions featuring photos of animals, typically canines, posed as if they are performing tasks associated with humans, in a similar vein to "Yes, This Is Dog" and the Dog Fort comic series.

name: Car Salesman Slaps Roof Of Car

text.visual_description: The scene depicts two primary characters: a salesman and a potential customer standing beside a car. The salesman is gesturing toward the car with an open palm, indicating a presentation or explanation, common in a sales scenario.
text.usage_text: Slaps Roof of Car is a popular phrasal template featuring a mock conversation between a car salesman and a potential buyer in which the salesman emphasizes the phrase "this bad boy can fit so much X in it" by slapping the roof of the car. The phrase is frequently used as the caption to an illustration of a car salesman and the buyer.

text.visual_description: The image features a penguin standing against a background divided into alternating red and pink diagonal segments, creating a dynamic backdrop. The penguin is captured mid-step, suggesting a sense of movement or action, as if it's walking away from or toward something.
text.usage_text: Socially Awesome Penguin is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photo of a penguin with a red color wheel background. As the antithesis of Socially Awkward Penguin, the captions depict the character as popular, charismatic, and sexually attractive.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this meme template presents a single male character depicted in a minimalist black-and-white line drawing, with no additional characters or entities visible. The individual’s prominent action is a wide-open smile with closed eyes, complemented by raised eyebrows.
text.usage_text: Yao Ming Face (sometimes referred to as "Fuck That Guy" or "Dumb Bitch") is a rage comic-style contour drawing of the professional basketball player Yao Ming wearing a hearty smile. The image is typically used as a reaction face to convey a dismissive attitude towards someone else's input in online discussions, usually following something that one-ups their input.

text.visual_description: The scene core features a human brain prominently displayed as the central entity, wearing a hat resembling a popular design patterned with a distinctive print. There are no visible characters or complex actions—only the brain sporting a hat, which stands out due to the humorous and unexpected nature of the combination.
text.usage_text: Scumbag Brain is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photo of a brain that is sometimes seen wearing the Scumbag Steve hat, with captions that describe self-conflicting psychological experiences like sudden realizations, awkward dreams, and persistent memories. The situations presented are similar to Oh God Why rage comics.

text.visual_description: The image depicts a chaotic scene with multiple race cars involved in a collision on a track. The cars are in various positions, some sideways or piled up, indicating a multi-car crash.
text.usage_text: Because "racecar" is a memetic phrase in which questions about cars are answered simply "because racecar." For example, if one asked, "Why doesn't that car have any trunk space?" then the other would reply, "Because racecar."

text.visual_description: The scene features a man from the 18th century with distinctive clothing, including a large hat, coat, and holding a walking stick. His body is angled toward the viewer, and he is pointing directly outward with a playful expression.
text.usage_text: Joseph Ducreux (June 26, 1735 – July 24, 1802) was an eighteenth-century French artist known for his unorthodox style of portrait paintings. On the internet, his eccentric self-portrait has inspired a series of exploitable macros, featuring "archaic reinterpretation" of popular rap lyrics superimposed over the artwork. Reminiscent of Bayeux Tapestry image macros, this highly verbose joke provides a satisfying challenge of "decoding" the corrupted lyrics back into the original verses.

name: Keep Calm And Carry On Red

text.visual_description: The image features a minimalistic red background with a white crown icon located at the top center. There is no visible text, leaving the design simple and stark.
text.usage_text: Keep Calm and Carry On is a catchphrase that originally appeared on a World War II-era British public safety poster. After one of the original posters was recovered and placed in a British bookshop in 2000, the inspirational message was shared online, sparking a series of image macros centered around the phrasal template "Keep Calm and X."

text.visual_description: The scene core features a single character, commonly known as Uncle Sam, depicted in a vintage style. He is a middle-aged man with a stern expression, wearing a top hat adorned with stars, a blue coat, and a red bowtie.
text.usage_text: The "I Want You" poster refers to the American war propaganda bill featuring the iconic image of Uncle Sam pointing his finger at the reader that was widely used to recruit soldiers during both World War I and World War II. Due to the massive scale of its distribution across the U.S. during the first half of the 20th century, the poster still remains culturally relevant to this day as one of the most recognizable American relics from the era.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this image features a close-up view of a smartphone screen held in a hand. The screen displays various app icons such as Videos, Maps, and FaceTime, which convey a typical smartphone interface.
text.usage_text: Donald Trump's Presidential Alert refers to a series of jokes based on a nationwide test of a presidential alert system built by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). Online, people posted mock messages from United States President Donald Trump.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this image features a small delivery truck with its cab tilted forward at an extreme angle, suggesting mechanical issues or maintenance work. The action involves no visible characters, as the image focuses solely on the truck itself within a somewhat deserted, open area.
text.usage_text: Sad Truck, also known as "Okay Truck," is an image macro series based on a picture of a white cargo truck with the driver's compartment lowered to the ground and various captions anthropomorphically depicting the truck as feeling depressed and ashamed.

text.visual_description: The image features a man sitting on a swing in a park, with two frames depicting consecutive moments. In both frames, he is holding a crumpled tissue to his face, suggesting he might be wiping away tears or trying to compose himself.
text.usage_text: First World Problems, also known as "White Whine," are frustrations and complaints that are only experienced by privileged individuals in wealthy countries. It is typically used as a tongue-in-cheek comedic device to make light of trivial inconveniences.

text.visual_description: The image features a stylized representation of the Google Chrome logo. The logo is depicted as a three-dimensional sphere divided into three segments, each in a distinct color: red, yellow, and green, circling around a central blue sphere.
text.usage_text: Google Chrome is a freeware web browser developed by Google that uses the WebKit layout engine. It was first released as a beta version for Microsoft Windows on September 2, 2008, and the public stable release was on December 11, 2008. As of June 2012, Google Chrome has 32.76% worldwide usage share of web browsers, making it the most widely used web browser, according to StatCounter. In September 2008, Google released a large portion of Chrome's source code as an open-source project called Chromium, which Chrome releases continue to be based on.

text.visual_description: The scene features a peculiar, anthropomorphic white creature resembling a cat, with large eyes, sitting on a box. There are no other characters present.
text.usage_text: Persian Room Cat Guardian is a reaction image macro series and Photoshop meme featuring photographs of a stuffed toy cat seated on top of a box with arms outstretched. Image macros of the photos are typically captioned with frustrating or annoying situations, using the stuffed toy's pose to convey an incredulous reaction.

text.visual_description: The meme template features a two-panel image. In the top panel, a young girl stands inside a home, leaning near a table with potted plants in the background.
text.usage_text: "Why Don't We Have Both?", also known as "Why Not Both?", is a reaction image and catchphrase that is used in response to various problems that involve choosing between two options or solutions.

text.visual_description: The image features a stern-looking figure in a military uniform, pointing directly at the viewer. The individual wears a drill instructor hat, adorned with various military badges and ribbons.
text.usage_text: Gunnery Sgt. Hartman is a fictional Marine Corps drill instructor played by actor R. Lee Ermey in the 1987 Stanley Kubrick war film Full Metal Jacket. Online, the character's iconic scenes in the film have spawned numerous remix and parody videos.

text.visual_description: The scene features a single person, centered in the image, against a plain white background. The individual is dressed in a casual white t-shirt, and there is a necklace visible around the neck.
text.usage_text: Ryan Gosling is a Canadian film actor who is known online for being the subject of several image macro series. These often involve photos of Gosling with a caption that begins with "Hey girl…"

text.visual_description: The scene features a character with long red hair, wearing glasses. The character's hands are raised near their face, suggesting a moment of realization or concern.
text.usage_text: Hipster Ariel (a.k.a. Hipster Mermaid) is an Advice Animal image macro series featuring a screenshot of Ariel from Disney's 1989 animated film The Little Mermaid and a superimposed caption poking fun at hipsterisms, in a similar vein to Hipster Kitty.

text.visual_description: The image features a man standing in an energetic pose in what appears to be a television studio filled with various financial and market-related paraphernalia. He is pointing forcefully to one side while surrounded by multiple screens and props such as toy bulls, emphasizing a financial theme.
text.usage_text: Mad Karma with Jim Cramer is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photoshopped image of Jim Cramer, former hedge fund manager and the host of the MSNBC business news program Mad Money. On Reddit, the character is often used as an indicator of an up-and-coming meme or a trending discussion topic, similar to the use of Imminent Ned and The Rent is Too Damn High.

text.visual_description: The image features a man wearing a light blue lab coat and a bow tie, standing with a skeleton model in the background. The man’s right hand is on his head, and he has an expression of surprise or realization.
text.usage_text: Bill Nye the Science Guy Remixes is a series of remix songs based on the theme song from the 1990s PBS children's educational show, Bill Nye the Science Guy. They often appear as recut music videos featuring footage from other memorable television shows, movies, or video games.

text.visual_description: The scene shows a character leaning back with an exaggerated motion, hands slightly raised, as though reacting to something unexpected. There is no visible text in the image.
text.usage_text: Dafuq is a slang interjection typically used in reaction to that which makes no sense or provokes severe confusion. It is short for the colloquial phrase "what the fuck?" and typically written without capital letters, spaces, and punctuation. Since appearing online in the late 2000s, the slang term has been used in memes, such as image macros, reaction images, and a commonly seen one with Snape from Harry Potter reacting in a shocked manner.

text.visual_description: The image features a single character, a woman with long blonde hair, who is centrally positioned and displaying a prominent smile. There are no other characters or complex actions taking place, as the focus is on her facial expression.
text.usage_text: Friend Zone Fiona is an advice animal image macro series with a stock photo of a laughing girl. The caption technique is similar to Successful Black Man, where the top text refers to something a girl would say romantically, followed by the bottom text confirming that she is just a friend.

text.visual_description: The image features a tall figure in a black suit with a white shirt and black tie, positioned at the center. This character is notable for its lack of facial features, presenting a blank, smooth surface where a face would normally be.
text.usage_text: Slender Man (a.k.a. Slenderman) is a mythical creature often depicted as a tall, thin figure wearing a black suit and a blank face. According to the legend, he can stretch or shorten his arms at will and has tentacle-like appendages protruding from his back. Depending on the interpretations of the myth, the creature may cause memory loss, insomnia, paranoia, coughing fits (nicknamed "slendersickness"), photograph/video distortions, and can teleport at will. The urban legend has inspired fan arts, fictional creepypastas, and a mockumentary series in the style of the 1999 indie horror film Blair Witch Project. As the character has grown in popularity, he's gained a number of other nicknames including The Operator, Der Großmann, Mr. Slim, The Administrator, Daddy Long Legs, Mr. Thin, The Tall Man, The Thin Man, and Slendy.

text.visual_description: The image features a black cat centered prominently, wearing a business-like yellow checkered tie on a white collar, set against a multi-colored radial background consisting of orange, green, red, blue, and tan segments. The cat is sitting upright, giving a composed and serious demeanor.
text.usage_text: Business Cat is an advice animal image macro series featuring a cat in a tie in front of a starburst background. The overlaid text usually includes something an office boss would do or request, but with a feline twist.

text.visual_description: The scene features a hand holding a cluster of purple grapes, each grape with a cartoonish, happy face. The background consists of what appears to be a staircase and a few objects, like a blue candle, indicating an indoor setting.
text.usage_text: Member Berries are a fictional superfruit that utter nostalgic, homophobic, and racist phrases to people while they are being eaten in Season 20, Episode 1 of the animated television series South Park.

text.visual_description: The scene features two comic-style characters depicted in a two-panel format. In the first panel, a character is shown saying, "He will never have a girlfriend," accompanied by a simple sketch of a person sitting and presumably speaking with a neutral to dismissive expression.
text.usage_text: Cereal Guy is a stick figure character commonly used on image boards and discussion forums as a multipurpose reaction face.

name: I Will Find You And Kill You

text.visual_description: The scene core features a single character presented in a dimly lit environment. The character is a middle-aged man with a serious demeanor, wearing a dark leather jacket.
text.usage_text: "I will find you, and I will kill you," also referred to as the Taken meme, is a memorable quote said by the protagonist character in the 2008 action-thriller movie Taken. Online, this phrase, along with other excerpts from the intense monologue, has been adopted as a phrasal template for heckling comments, most typically in the form of reaction images.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this meme template features a single, highly stylized cartoon face known as the "trollface." The character displays exaggerated facial features, including an enormous grin that stretches across the entire face, with heavily arched eyebrows and half-closed eyes. The image is purely black and white, with bold lines defining the face’s comically mischievous expression.
text.usage_text: Trollface is a rage comic character wearing a mischievous smile that is meant to represent the facial expression of an Internet troll. The image is most commonly used to portray a character as a troll in rage comics, or alternatively, to identify oneself or another participant as such in online discussions.

text.visual_description: The scene core features the prominent head of a chicken set against a background with alternating pink and orange diagonal rays. There are no additional characters or entities, and no visible text accompanies the image.
text.usage_text: Anti-Joke Chicken is an image macro series featuring an image of a hen accompanied by a top line of text that sounds like the introduction of a joke, but the bottom line provides an unexpected anticlimax. The chicken is centered within a typical advice animal starburst background.

text.visual_description: Scene Core: The image depicts a man sipping from a pint of beer, sitting in what appears to be an outdoor café or pub. The main character is casually dressed and seems to be enjoying his drink, with a relaxed setting signaled by other patrons in the background sitting at tables.
text.usage_text: Lazy College Senior is an advice animal image macro series featuring a young man with short, disheveled brown hair drinking a pint of beer. The images are typically captioned with unmotivated statements or behaviors that are associated with burnt-out college students during their final year of school, a phenomenon commonly known as “senioritis.” The character can be seen as the antithesis of College Freshman.

text.visual_description: The image features two main visual components of the same character: one is a focused or serious-looking portrait, while the other shows the person in a martial arts stance. The portrait is a large, semi-transparent background figure, and the stance is highlighted in the foreground.
text.usage_text: Karate Kyle is an advice animal image macro series similar to Vengeance Dad and PTSD Clarinet Boy, where the original photo consists of a digital composite of the subject's head enlarged around his entire body with the opacity decreased. The captions generally depict various violent acts Karate Kyle has performed in retaliation for being bullied.

text.visual_description: The scene features a young woman with exaggerated makeup that creates a ghostly appearance, characterized by dark circles around her eyes and a wide, toothy grin. The visual contrast between her pale face and the dark makeup highlights her facial features, drawing attention to her eyes and smile.
text.usage_text: Overly Attached Girlfriend is an advice animal image macro featuring a webcam picture of vlogger Laina Morris and various captions portraying her in the stereotype of an overprotective and clingy girlfriend.

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image contains the head of a Shiba Inu dog, centered against a background divided into colorful, radial segments of pink, purple, blue, green, yellow, and orange. There is no visible text.
text.usage_text: Advice Dog is an image macro series that features a picture of the head of a smiling puppy on a color wheel background split into six separate colors. Usual derivatives are often accompanied by two lines of text written in a guidance or advising format, with the advice given usually being very poor, unethical, or deplorable. Since its debut, the series has spawned dozens of spin-offs referred to as Advice Animals. In these variations, memers replace the dog's head with a different animal's or a human's head, adding advice that is reflective of the character's archetype personality and using the same two-line image macro formula.

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image consists of a cat riding a unicorn. The unicorn is prominently positioned, rearing up on its hind legs with a majestic mane and a glowing horn, while the cat is standing upright, holding a golden firearm.
text.usage_text: "Welcome to the Internet" is a catchphrase used to genuinely welcome someone to navigating the web itself or to internet culture. Alternatively, it can be used as a sarcastic insult to mock those who are not familiar with how internet culture works, for example, in response to someone being disgusted by something they saw online or reposted outdated content. It is commonly found as a caption on image macros and GIFs, sometimes paired with the phrase "I will be your guide."

text.visual_description: The image features a person in a black suit and sunglasses performing a distinctive dance move known as the "horse-riding dance." The setting appears to be a stable, evidenced by the presence of horses on either side. There is no visible text in the image.
text.usage_text: Gangnam Style (강남 스타일) is a 2012 dance pop single written and performed by Korean pop singer Park Jae Sung, better known by his stage name PSY. Since its release in mid-July 2012, the highly entertaining music video has spawned hundreds of parodies and copycat dance videos on YouTube and surpassed Justin Bieber's single "Baby" as the most watched video on YouTube with over one billion views as of December 21st, 2012.

text.visual_description: The image features a young woman with long brown hair, standing outdoors with a blurred background. She is smiling broadly, which is the focal point of the scene.
text.usage_text: Rebecca Black is an amateur YouTube musician who soared into the public eye for her music video "Friday." The song gained significant online notoriety in March 2011 for its monotonous lyrics accompanied by heavy use of auto-tune.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts a young boy in bed, partially covered by a blanket. His face is the central focus, expressing fear or distress.
text.usage_text: "I see dead people" is a memorable quote from the 1999 supernatural horror film The Sixth Sense. On the web, both the original line and its snowclone variations have been used to mock a particular group of people for their behaviors or stereotypes.

name: If You Know What I Mean Bean

text.visual_description: The scene core of this meme template features a black and white line drawing of a man in a suit with thick, slicked-back hair. The character is tilting his head slightly forward and to the side, with a mischievous smirk on his face.
text.usage_text: "If You Know What I Mean" is a rage comic character based on a still frame of actor Rowan Atkinson portraying the fictional character Mr. Bean. It is used to point out a double entendre in a post or image macro, commonly in the form of sexual innuendo. Although originally created as a rage face, the character is also used in vertical comics in a similar manner to the "You Don't Say?" and "We've Got a Badass Over Here" reaction images.

text.visual_description: The image features a simple visual element: a stylized flag icon, typically associated with social media safety notifications. The flag is blue, signifying a generic indication of safety status.
text.usage_text: Marked Safe From X is an exploitable image and phrasal template that parodies the Facebook Crisis Response status updates that are usually deployed after a disaster or dangerous event. The Safety Check feature's first major deployment was on April 25th, 2015, in the aftermath of the Nepal earthquake. The "marked safe from X today" status featuring the blue flag graphic began to be parodied in 2017, with early memes marking themselves as "safe" from various people or places.

text.visual_description: The scene features two cows in a grassy field with a significant fire blazing in the background. The cows are positioned in the foreground, facing the viewer, while the fire dominates the backdrop.
text.usage_text: Evil Cows is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photo of two cows standing in front of a burned-down building, similar in composition to the original Disaster Girl photograph. Like PTSD Clarinet Kid and Vengeance Dad, Evil Cows image macros are captioned with first-person confessions of vengeful deeds but often include references to the farming and fast food industries.

text.visual_description: The image depicts a professional male newscaster seated at a news desk. He is dressed in a dark suit and tie, with a microphone visible clipped to his jacket, indicating that he is in a broadcast setting.
text.usage_text: #BrianWilliamsMisremembers is a Twitter hashtag and photoshop meme featuring the American news anchor and managing editor of NBC Nightly News, Brian Williams, which began in February 2015 following the revelation of the journalist's false claims about his time he spent in Iraq. The photoshopped images commonly feature Williams present in notable historic events.

text.visual_description: The image features a man with a rugged appearance, guns in both hands, wearing a sleeveless denim shirt and jeans. He stands with legs apart in a confident, action-oriented stance.
text.usage_text: Chuck Norris, born Carlos Ray "Chuck" Norris on March 10th, 1940, is a martial artist, actor, and culture star. Chuck Norris is mostly known for his roles in the TV series Walker, Texas Ranger, as well as The Way of the Dragon, where he played alongside Bruce Lee.

text.visual_description: In the scene core, the main character is a solitary man sitting on a bench outdoors, in what appears to be an urban setting. He is holding a sandwich while staring down at a small bird walking near his feet.
text.usage_text: Sad Keanu is a Photoshop meme based on a paparazzi photograph of the Canadian-American actor Keanu Reeves sitting on a park bench and enjoying a sandwich by himself.

text.visual_description: Scene Core: The main character in this image is a white, fluffy creature with a humanoid posture, sitting on a box. Its body is covered with fur, and it has a face that resembles a cat with exaggerated, wide eyes and a small mouth.
text.usage_text: Persian Room Cat Guardian is a reaction image macro series and photoshop meme featuring photographs of a stuffed toy cat seated on top of a box with arms outstretched. Image macros of the photos are typically captioned with frustrating or annoying situations, using the stuffed toy's pose to convey an incredulous reaction.

text.visual_description: The image features a close-up of a man's face, captured with exaggerated expressions that draw immediate attention. There are no other visible characters or entities in the frame.
text.usage_text: Impossibru is a reaction image based on a still shot of an Asian man wearing a bizarre expression and the caption reading "impossibru," which is typically interpreted as the Engrish equivalent of the word "impossible" (Japanese: インポシブル imposhiburu). Both the image and the phrase have been used to express one's surprise or exclamation across various forums and imageboard sites, and is notable as being similar to Rape Face.

text.visual_description: In the image, the core scene centers around a cartoon character that appears to be a red crab-like figure placed in the foreground. This character is surrounded by a blurred crowd of various other characters, suggesting a hectic or confusing environment.
text.usage_text: Confused Mr. Krabs refers to a reaction image of the Spongebob Squarepants character Mr. Krabs with a confused expression as the world around him spins. The image is popular as a companion to jokes that indicate the poster is confused.

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image features a close-up of a man's face with a layered colorful background divided into triangular segments, including green, pink, orange, and yellow hues. The primary character is positioned centrally, with no additional characters or text present in the image.
text.usage_text: Butthurt Dweller, also known as "Gordo Granudo," is an image macro series that features a photo of a young adult male with a ponytail and glasses accompanied by overlaid text that involves a smug or judgmental statement.

name: The Most Interesting Cat In The World

text.visual_description: The meme template image features a cat as the central character, reclining confidently on a cat tree. The cat’s posture is relaxed yet self-assured, with its front paw draped over the edge of the perch.
text.usage_text: The Most Interesting Cat In The World is an image macro featuring a cat with its arm around a seat in a relaxed pose similar to Cool Dog. The overlaid text usually follows a style of "I don't always X, but when I do, I Y." This is a spin-off of The Most Interesting Man in the World, usually with a theme of cat ownership annoyances.

text.visual_description: The image features two characters engaged in an embrace. One character’s face is visible with a neutral, slightly pensive expression.
text.usage_text: "I Know That Feel Bro" (also known as "to uczucie" or "to uczucie") is an Internet slang expression used to convey empathy towards or agree with someone else's feeling or opinion. The expression, which roughly means "I feel you, bro," is typically accompanied by a contour-drawing reaction image of two bald men embracing each other expressionlessly. The face has been used as an exploitable character and is often seen in "that feel when" (TFW) threads on image boards, which describe an emotional situation or event.

text.visual_description: The scene features the face of a golden retriever puppy positioned at the center of a radiant background. The puppy's mouth is open, with ears perked and eyes wide open, giving an impression of excitement or happiness.
text.usage_text: Advice Dog is an image macro series that features a picture of the head of a smiling puppy on a color wheel background split into six separate colors. Usual derivatives are often accompanied by two lines of text written in a guidance or advising format with the advice given usually being very poor, unethical, or deplorable. Since its debut, the series has spawned dozens of spin-offs referred to as Advice Animals. In these variations, memers replace the dog's head with a different animal's or a human's head, adding advice that is reflective of the character's archetype personality and using the same two-line image macro formula.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts a man with a bearded face, clad in a blue plaid shirt, positioned prominently in the foreground. He appears to be sitting in a dimly lit environment, with a soft focus on the background, which includes patterned objects that are indistinct but add complexity to the scene.
text.usage_text: Dating Site Murderer, sometimes known as "Good Intentions Axe Murderer," is an advice animal image macro series based on a dimly lit photograph of a bearded Redditor. The captions typically employ the bait-and-switch scheme similar to the Successful Black Man series: the top line implies murderous intent, while the bottom line brings a twist of something innocuous and sweet.

text.visual_description: The scene features a single character, a man wearing a distinctive mask that covers his mouth and nose. He is dressed in a dark coat, standing in what appears to be a dimly lit space with bars or a cage-like structure in the background.
text.usage_text: "When Gotham is ashes, you have my permission to die" is a quote from the 2012 superhero action film The Dark Knight Rises, uttered by the primary antagonist, Bane. Shortly after the film's release in July 2012, the quote soon emerged as one of the more memorable lines and evolved into a snowclone, spawning variations based on the phrasal templates "You have my permission to X" or "When Y, you have my permission to die."

text.visual_description: The scene centers on a muscular individual striking a powerful pose with both arms flexed, showcasing strength and confidence. The person is adorned with numerous gold chains and rings, adding a sense of opulence and flamboyance to the image.
text.usage_text: Around the late 1990s, one of the more absurd items you could find on the web was a series of standalone websites dedicated to Mr. T taking on a notable person or character. The sites usually presented the story in a multi-page comic-book format using crude photo edits that combined the same stock images of Mr. T with the villain of the day. The results always had Mr. T coming out the winner, but the draw was in the storytelling of how Mr. T came into the fight and how he went about it.

text.visual_description: The image depicts two cartoon men, both in professional attire. The man on the left is extending his right arm as if presenting something or gesturing towards an idea.
text.usage_text: Slaps roof of car is a popular phrasal template featuring a mock conversation between a car salesman and a potential buyer in which the salesman emphasizes the phrase "this bad boy can fit so much X in it" by slapping the roof of the car. The phrase is frequently used as the caption to an illustration of a car salesman and the buyer.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts a set of white plastic outdoor furniture, consisting of a square table and four chairs, situated on a neatly mowed green lawn. Three chairs are arranged upright around the table, while one chair lies on its side, seemingly toppled over.
text.usage_text: We Will Rebuild refers to a series of images of minor objects which have fallen over or been knocked slightly out of place, sarcastically captioned with the slogan "We will rebuild" in reference to a typically insignificant natural disaster. It is similar to, and is often used interchangeably with, the sarcastic use of "never forget."

text.visual_description: The image features the head of a frog at the center, set against a background of intersecting green triangles of varying shades. The frog appears realistic and is the primary focus, providing a clear and distinct visual contrast with the geometric background.
text.usage_text: Foul Bachelor Frog is an advice animal image macro series featuring a frog's face in front of a color wheel background containing various shades of green. The images' captions often depict lazy, disgusting, and hedonistic behaviors associated with single men.

text.visual_description: The scene features one main character: a man standing in a casual setting, possibly a porch or a backyard. He is holding a bottle in one hand and gesturing with the other hand in a thumbs-up pose.
text.usage_text: Redneck Randal is an advice animal image macro series centered around a picture of a mustached young man wearing a sleeveless American pride T-shirt and posing with two thumbs up. The captions typically involve poking fun at the lifestyle of so-called American "rednecks," a derogatory slang term for people from the Southern United States associated with unabashed American pride, beer drinking, and rural life.

text.visual_description: Scene Core: The main character in the image is a cat peeking through a small, square hole in the ceiling. The cat’s face is partially visible, with its head tilted down as if looking into the room below.
text.usage_text: Ceiling Cat is a Photoshop meme based on a photograph of a cat peeking through a hole in the ceiling of a room. Its online popularity eventually led to several derivative characters, including his nemesis, Basement Cat and Basement Horse.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts a man driving a convertible car on a sunny day, with his gaze fixed ahead. He wears a black and white patterned shirt and a black beanie.
text.usage_text: "It Was a Good Day" is an image macro series featuring a screen capture of the rapper Ice Cube driving a car, accompanied by captions recalling positive events that conclude with "It was a good day."

text.visual_description: The scene features two main characters, an elderly man with a long white beard and glasses, wearing ornate robes and a distinctive cap, and a younger person facing him. The action involves the older man leaning forward, intensely engaging with the young person.
text.usage_text: Dumbledore Asked Calmly, also known as Did You Put Your Name In the Goblet of Fire, refers to a humorous discrepancy between a scene from the 2000 fantasy novel Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire and the corresponding scene from the 2005 film of the same name. In the book, Dumbledore is described as behaving calmly, while in the film the character is shown interrogating the main protagonist, Harry Potter, in a highly agitated manner. The discrepancy spawned multiple memes and parodies in the Harry Potter community.

text.visual_description: The image features a wet koala that appears startled or aggressive. It is situated among green foliage, likely in a natural setting.
text.usage_text: Wet Koala refers to a viral image of a wet koala bear photoshopped to appear angry and with its jaw wide open, revealing a set of sharp teeth. The photoshop, as well as an image macro using it, was initially circulated in 2012 as people believed it was authentic, resurfacing numerous times over the next decade.

text.visual_description: The scene features a solitary person gazing out of a window, their hand pressed against the glass. It is a black and white image, which contributes to a somber mood.
text.usage_text: Over-Educated Problems is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photograph of a man glumly looking out a window onto a rainy street. As a spin-off of the First World Problems series, the captions typically include frustrations associated with being "too well educated" compared to one's peers.

text.visual_description: The scene features a young child sitting at a table in a high chair. The child is holding a spoon in one hand and a toy phone to their ear with the other, against a backdrop of a cozy kitchen or dining area.
text.usage_text: Business Baby is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photograph of a toddler talking on a toy phone with captions depicting the child as an enterprising business executive.

text.visual_description: Scene Core: The image features the head of a wolf with a ferocious expression against a radiant, contrasting background of yellow and orange rays. The wolf's eyes are wide and focused, showing intensity, and its mouth is open, exposing sharp teeth.
text.usage_text: Courage Wolf is an image macro series derived from the original Advice Dog series. In contrast to Advice Dog, who might unknowingly lead you to do something you'll regret, Courage Wolf will help you achieve greatness with often extreme, overwhelming advice.

text.visual_description: The image features a single male character wearing a white cap and a light-colored shirt, with his hands on his hips. The background is a series of radiating, contrasting earthy tones that draw attention to the central figure.
text.usage_text: Ordinary Muslim Man is an advice animal image macro series featuring a smiling man wearing a Muslim taqiyah hat. The images are typically accompanied by bait-and-switch captions with an initial statement that can be perceived as anti-American, followed by a phrase that renders the statement innocuous (see also Successful Black Man).

name: I Have No Idea What I Am Doing Dog

text.visual_description: The image features a golden retriever surrounded by laboratory glassware filled with various colored liquids, including beakers and a flask attached to a stand. The dog is wearing a pair of safety goggles on its head, which adds a whimsical and humorous twist to the scenario.
text.usage_text: "I Have No Idea What I'm Doing" is a catchphrase often used in image macro captions featuring photos of animals, typically canines, posed as if they are performing tasks associated with humans, in a similar vein to "Yes, This is Dog" and the Dog Fort comic series.

text.visual_description: The scene features a cat lying on its back on a bed, dressed in overalls. The cat’s posture is relaxed, with its limbs spread out casually, and there is no visible text in the image.
text.usage_text: BODE refers to images with the word "BODE" (short for "bodacious") overlaid on them. The images often are of overweight cats and cat-like creatures and are popular mostly on Tumblr.

text.visual_description: The image depicts an animated seal with a simplistic, cartoonish design set against a plain background. The seal is the sole character, captured mid-motion as it appears to be pointing or gesturing with its flipper towards something outside of the frame.
text.usage_text: Homophobic Seal (also known as "Gay Seal") is a webcomic character that is known for its catchphrase "GAAAAAAYYYY." It is often added to the bottom of an image to dismiss everything above as naive, weak, or saccharine.

text.visual_description: The scene core comprises two main characters in close proximity, with one character being more visible. The visible character appears to be a pirate with long hair and a bandana, engaged in a dynamic conversation or confrontation.
text.usage_text: Why is the rum gone? is a popular meme based on the line from the hit movie Pirates of the Caribbean: Curse of the Black Pearl. The line became an instant classic as fans began using it in images and videos.

text.visual_description: The image features a prominent blue parrot with vibrant orange eyes positioned against a distinctive background of green and orange triangles converging at the center. The parrot's head is slightly tilted, showcasing its feather details and strong beak.
text.usage_text: Paranoid Parrot is an advice animal image macro series featuring a blue and yellow parrot looking over its shoulder. The captions often relay a mundane scenario or an everyday situation (e.g., "save game file") followed by an irrational response driven by paranoia.

text.visual_description: The image presents an older man, likely a farmer or rancher, as suggested by his attire, consisting of a cowboy hat and a quilted vest. He is leaning on a fence, with one arm resting casually atop it, which contributes to the rural, outdoors setting.
text.usage_text: "So God Made a Farmer" is the title of a speech given by the late American radio personality Paul Harvey at the Future Farmers of America convention in 1978. Following the airing of a Dodge Ram commercial set to the audio recording of the speech during Super Bowl XLVII in February 2013, parodies of the commercial and the speech based on other occupations, races, or subcultures began appearing on YouTube.

text.visual_description: The scene features two main figures at an event, one holding a microphone and gesturing emphatically, and the other holding a trophy with a surprised expression. The individual with the microphone seems to be interrupting the situation, while the trophy holder appears to be taken off guard.
text.usage_text: Kanye Interrupts, also known as "Imma let you finish," refers to an on-air mishap that occurred during Taylor Swift's acceptance speech for Best Female Video at the 2009 MTV Video Music Awards. During the speech, Kanye West suddenly went up to the stage and took the microphone from Swift to declare that Beyonce had "one of the best music videos of all time."

text.visual_description: The image features a giant panda leaning casually on a tree stump with a bottle placed next to it, giving the impression the panda is relaxing or taking a break. The radial background features alternating shades of gray, drawing the observer’s focus towards the center where the panda is positioned.
text.usage_text: Pick Up Line Panda is an advice animal image macro series based on a picture of a panda bear standing by a tree stump with a beer bottle. The captioned jokes typically begin with a predictable pickup cliché followed by a sentence that is contrasted by lack of subtlety.

text.visual_description: The scene features a young man sitting outdoors, possibly on a college campus, given the brick buildings and autumn foliage in the background. He is wearing a grey hoodie with "UNH" printed on it, and has a backpack strapped on.
text.usage_text: College Freshman (a.k.a. Uber Frosh) is an image macro series featuring a college student with headphones, a University of New Hampshire hoodie, and a mobile phone. Portrayed as a hybrid of Scumbag Steve and Socially Awkward Penguin, the captions usually highlight the all-too-familiar clichés found in campus social scenes and student life during college years.

text.visual_description: The meme template features a cartoonish pink creature resembling a Pokémon known for its sluggish nature. It is positioned against a vibrant, radial background with alternating shades of magenta and pink, which draws immediate visual attention.
text.usage_text: Slowpoke is a Pokémon-themed reaction image response popularized on 4chan as a way to troll other users. The accompanying text often uses the line "Hey guys, did you hear…" before presenting a piece of old or oversaturated information.

text.visual_description: The scene core features a simple, monochrome, stick-figure drawing with a large, circular head and minimalist facial features. The main character is depicted with a slightly turned-up mouth, raised eyebrows, and narrowed eyes, creating a smug or self-satisfied expression.
text.usage_text: "Challenge Accepted" is an expression used to indicate that the speaker is willing to attempt completing a difficult task. The phrase is often associated with a rage comic character illustrated as a stick figure with crossed arms and a smug facial expression.

text.visual_description: The image features a cartoon character's head with gray hair and pronounced eyebrows, set against a vibrant, radiating background of blue, red, and gray stripes. The character appears to be male, exhibiting a stern and focused expression.
text.usage_text: Professor Oak, sometimes referred to as Advice Oak, is an image macro series featuring the face of Pokémon character Professor Oak, which is used to point out the various illogical details about the video game's world, also known as video game logic, and the alleged jerkish behavior of the character. Appearing in the form of an Advice Animal meme similar to Advice Dog, this format also uses a color wheel background with top and bottom text captions.

name: Keep Calm And Carry On Black

text.visual_description: The image consists of a simple design featuring a stylized white crown against a black background. There are no characters or actions taking place in this template, and the crown is the key visual element that stands out prominently.
text.usage_text: Keep Calm and Carry On is a catchphrase that originally appeared on a World War II-era British public safety poster. After one of the original posters was recovered and placed in a British bookshop in 2000, the inspirational message was shared online, sparking a series of image macros centered around the phrasal template "Keep Calm and X."

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image features a cartoon character with an exaggerated facial expression, large eyes, and tears streaming down its face. The character's hands are held up to its mouth in a gesture that suggests surprise or overwhelming emotion.
text.usage_text: Cuteness Overload is a reaction face drawn in the style of a rage comic character, often used to depict the emotional responses after seeing babies or animals that are deemed adorable, a sad story, or a heartwarming moment.

text.visual_description: In this image, the main character is a woman who appears to be crying, with a hand resting on her head, a gesture that indicates distress or frustration. There is no visible text present in the image.
text.usage_text: First World Problems, also known as "White Whine," are frustrations and complaints that are only experienced by privileged individuals in wealthy countries. It is typically used as a tongue-in-cheek comedic device to make light of trivial inconveniences.

name: He Will Never Get A Girlfriend

text.visual_description: The image features a simple, black-and-white stick-figure character engaged in an animated talking gesture, seated in front of what seems to be a table with scattered items. The character exhibits an assertive posture, with one arm outstretched forward and the other slightly raised.
text.usage_text: "He Will Never Have a Girlfriend" (alt: "She Will Never Have a Boyfriend") is a series of multi-pane rage comics featuring Cereal Guy's reaction to pre-fame and post-fame comparison photographs of well-known celebrities. In 2019, the format resurged on the /r/okbuddyretard subreddit as an ironic meme.

text.visual_description: The scene features a single character, a man with curly hair and facial hair, who appears to be wearing a suit. The character is caught mid-expression, with wide eyes and an open mouth, suggesting he's in the middle of speaking or reacting strongly to something off-camera.
text.usage_text: English, Motherfucker, Do You Speak It? is a famous catchphrase spoken by actor Samuel L. Jackson in the 1994 Quentin Tarantino movie Pulp Fiction. The line became a commonly used catchphrase online and resulted in numerous memes over the course of the 2000s, including but not limited to image macros, photoshops, and demotivational posters. Similarly, the lines "Does He Look Like A Bitch?" and "Say 'What' Again I Double Dare You," taken from the same scene, have seen similar popularization.

text.usage_text: Nailed It is a phrase used to express success after achieving something seemingly difficult with relative ease. Online, it is often found as a caption on image macros or in sarcastic commentary criticizing the quality of success, especially in response to attempts at recreating recipes or craft projects.

text.visual_description: The image features a family portrait with three main characters: a woman, a young boy, and a young girl, all smiling warmly. They are positioned together in the foreground, conveying familial closeness.
text.usage_text: Vengeance Dad is an image macro series based on a digitally composited family photograph of a balding father on the right side and presumably the mother and two children on the left side. In a similar style to PTSD Clarinet Kid, Vengeance Dad images are captioned with first-person style confessions as if he is recounting a terrible event that happened to his family due to his own fault or intent.

text.usage_text: Obama Rage Face (also known as "Not Bad" Face) is a rage comic reaction face based on a press photograph of Barack Obama wearing a stoic face during his official state visit to the United Kingdom in May 2011. The image is used as a positive response to a pleasant surprise or an outcome of an event that has surpassed one's expectation, similar to the usage of the "everything went better than expected" face.

text.usage_text: Dat Alarm Clock, or in a case, Dat X Clock (where X is the name of the video game/character/show the sound clip originated) is a video format meme that consists of the Family Guy video clip playing at the point where the alarm clock (a Palestinian alarm clock, stated in the original episode) in the video changes to 7:00. As stated before, an audio clip of choice is played, and then the video ends with the clock exploding. This meme was sought out by many, most of whom used different audio clips to remix the video, and gained some popularity.

text.usage_text: Laundry Room Viking is an advice animal image macro series based on a Facebook photo of a guy treading his way through a flooded laundry room after Hurricane Irene in August 2011. Echoing the original caption, "Do the laundry, they said. It will be fun, they said," the series usually juxtaposes an overly optimistic statement quoted by someone else against the undesirable conditions in reality.

text.usage_text: Insanity Puppy is an advice animal image macro series of a Siberian Husky puppy with markings reminiscent of a cartoon villain. He is depicted as a younger version of Insanity Wolf, similar to Baby Courage Pup. The text often consists of an over-the-top or psychotic reaction to something.

text.usage_text: Rasta Science Teacher (a.k.a. Rasta Professor) is an image macro series based on a picture of a class instructor wearing dreadlocks and a Rasta fashion hat. A type of bait-and-switch joke involving intentional line breaks similar to Dating Site Murderer and Successful Black Man, the captions usually consist of two parts: 1) a direct reference to Reggae songs or smokers' lingo and 2) an anticlimactic statement derailing to academic subjects in the manner of a science teacher.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts an intense and dramatic image of a large explosion, likely a nuclear explosion, characterized by a massive mushroom cloud dominating the entire frame. The main visual elements include the bright orange and yellow hues of fire and smoke rising from the base, with dark silhouettes of the surrounding landscape providing scale.
text.usage_text: What the F-Bomb, also known as WTF Boom or WTFBoom, is a series of video memes in which a normal event gets interrupted by a loud voice screaming "WHAT THE F-" cut off by an extremely loud explosion and a sinister laugh. It is commonly used as an element of surprise or interruption. The audio clip has also been used by VideoCompiler in a number of his "Ventrilo harassment" videos in which he hacks into user Ventrilo servers, harasses users with soundbites and posts videos online for lulz. It is commonly called the "WTF Boom/Bomb" on YouTube.

text.usage_text: Mother of God... is a rage comic character of a man staring intently at something as he takes his sunglasses off. It can also be used outside of rage comics to express astonishment or disbelief in response to a shocking image or a video. Similar to the colloquial usage of the phrase, the reaction face can be used to either indicate approval or disapproval, depending on the context. When used in the context of rage comics, it is usually preceded by a stick-figure drawing of the same man humming and walking with sunglasses still on.

text.usage_text: Woah Vicky is the online handle of teenage social media personality Victoria Waldrip. In 2022, Waldrip refound Christianity and started posting more about her religion online. In 2023, Waldrip was a cast member on the reality series Baddies East but left after five episodes, allegedly due to an altercation with cast member Janet.

text.usage_text: "Y'all Got Any More of…" is an expression typically used on discussion forums to request additional information on a particular topic of interest, or more generally, to indicate one's intense craving for something. Originally quoted by the drug-fiending character Tyrone Biggums in Chappelle's Show, the phrase is often iterated as a reaction image or image macro format based on a still shot of Dave Chappelle's character and the phrasal template "Y'all got any more of them / X?"

text.usage_text: Lame Pun Raccoon, also known as "Pun Coon" or "Bad Joke Raccoon," is an image macro series centered around a happy-looking raccoon that utters various puns for the sake of witticism. The first Nicktoon, the show has experienced a resurgence of popularity online due to the increase in '90s nostalgia.

text.usage_text: Ridiculously Photogenic Guy (RPG) is a Photoshop meme and advice animal featuring a photo of a smiling man called Zeddie Little running in the 2012 Cooper River Bridge Run. text.usage_text: Hasta La Vista, Zombie refers to a series of memes based on a three-panel image macro depicting Rick Grimes (played by actor Andrew Lincoln) from The Walking Dead aiming his gun at a zombie and saying, "Hasta la vista zombie," in the first panel, the zombie then telling Grimes he likes something in the second, followed by Grimes and the zombie posing for a photo together after the zombie successfully convinces Grimes not to shoot her. The original meme was posted to Facebook as early as 2017 and became the subject of photoshops over the following years, often altering the caption associated with the zombie.

text.usage_text: Idiot Nerd Girl is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photo of a teenage girl wearing thick-rimmed glasses with the word "NERD" written on the palm of her left hand. text.usage_text: Keep Calm and Carry On is a catchphrase that originally appeared on a World War II-era British public safety poster. text.usage_text: Fuck Yeah is a series of four-pane cartoon strips featuring a stick figure looking complacent and confident. Originally posted via /b/ board in February 2010, these cartoons illustrate triumphant moments. This phenomenon can also be seen as the antithesis to Rage Guy comics, another four-pane series originating from 4chan circa late 2008.

text.usage_text: The LZ 129 Hindenburg was a German passenger airship which exploded over New Jersey on May 6th, 1937. The disaster was famously observed by, among others, radio journalist Herbert Morrison, who very melodramatically described it in a narration famously played together with a separate filming of the event, forming what has since become the definitive audio-visual account. Morrison's speech contains the now-famous phrase "Oh, the humanity," which has since become a commonly repeated quote used to express shock and awe at disastrous events.
